questions.q: What are the five stages of the data quality lifecycle, in order, per this lesson?
options: Profile, define, measure, remediate, monitor
Define, profile, remediate, measure, monitor
Measure, remediate, profile, define, monitor
Monitor, profile, define, measure, remediate
questions.explain: The lifecycle runs: profile (discover what's there) → define (turn findings into rules) → measure (run the rules) → remediate (fix problems) → monitor (watch continuously).

questions.q: Why does this lesson call the data quality lifecycle 'a loop, not a checklist you finish once'?
options: Because new data keeps arriving and systems keep changing, which resets the cycle back to profiling again
Because each stage must be repeated exactly three times before completion
Because the five stages have no particular order and can be done in any sequence
Because only the 'monitor' stage ever needs to be repeated
questions.explain: New source systems, new fields, and changed business rules mean the loop runs continuously rather than completing as a one-time project.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the most common mistake teams make in this lifecycle?
options: Skipping the 'profile' stage and writing rules from assumption instead of what the data actually contains
Spending too much time monitoring and not enough time defining rules
Remediating problems before they are ever measured
Running the 'measure' stage too many times
questions.explain: Jumping straight to 'define' without profiling first leads to rules based on assumption (like 'phone numbers are always 10 digits') that fail against real data.

questions.q: In the 'measure' stage, why does this lesson emphasize running rules 'repeatedly' rather than once?
options: Because a single clean pass means nothing if quality silently degrades over the following month
Because SQL Server requires queries to be run multiple times to return correct results
Because each rule can only check one row per execution
Because repetition is required to satisfy regulatory compliance in every industry
questions.explain: Measurement needs to be ongoing and tracked over time, not a single pass, since data quality can degrade after an initial clean check.

questions.q: Which chapter of this course is entirely dedicated to the 'profile' stage of the lifecycle?
options: Chapter 2
Chapter 3
Chapter 4
Chapter 5
questions.explain: Chapter 2 (Lessons 6-10), starting immediately after this lesson, is dedicated entirely to profiling techniques.
